results.title: Tesla launches FSD v15, targets its biggest weaknesses, from signs to potholes | Electrek
results.content:
> v15 upgrades every part of the end-to-end driving network. Includes:
> 
> Upgraded vision encoder shared between FSD, Robotaxi, and Optimus, which is trained on millions of internet videos for improved generalization and data efficiency, improving the critical intervention rate by 25x.
> 
> Introduced Tesla Augmented Reality, replacing all of the explicit model signals into a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.
> 
> Improved navigation by using an end-to-end learned model based on route preference data from the fleet.
> 
> Improved parking location selection by using personalized parking history, and the map will now display multiple parking options at your destination.
> [...] Tesla calls it “Reality View” in its announcement and “Tesla Augmented Reality” in the release notes. The notes say it replaces all the separate model signals with a single end-to-end visualization that uses less compute, and Tesla says it lets the driver “see & control what FSD is planning to do.” If that works as advertised, it could make supervising the system a lot easier.

## v15 goes after FSD’s biggest weak spots

What stands out more is where Tesla is focusing. Almost every driving improvement in the release notes targets an area where FSD struggles today.

results.title: Tesla Rolls Out FSD v15 Featuring 25x Better Handling of Critical Safety, Reality View, and More Upgrades
results.content:
Tesla's Full Self-Driving software has been getting steadily smarter with each release, but the latest version being pushed out to eligible vehicles carries some of the most consequential upgrades the system has seen in a while.

The headline claim is dramatic, and the company has explained exactly how it arrived at the number.

## Tesla Rolls Out FSD v15 to Eligible EVs

Tesla began rolling out Full Self-Driving version 15 to eligible vehicles on November 21, 2026, posting the initial announcement through its official X account with a brief breakdown of what the update brings. The company described v15 as upgrading every part of the end-to-end driving network, covering safety, visualization, navigation, environmental awareness, and new driving modes. [...] Bike Rack Mode is a new addition for drivers who tow bike racks or similar hitch accessories. When activated, FSD operates differently near the destination, pulling over rather than reversing, and disabling Autopark, Summon, and the associated backup chimes and warnings that would otherwise conflict with the extended rear profile of the vehicle.

Tesla also confirmed that future v15 updates will allow FSD-capable Tesla vehicles to be added to the Robotaxi fleet, a step toward the company's longer-term vision of network-based autonomous ride-hailing using privately owned Tesla vehicles. That capability was not included in the initial v15 release and will arrive in a subsequent update. [...] Navigation improvements in v15 extend to both ends of the route. The route selection at the start and end of a trip now learns from fleet route preferences, pulling on what other drivers have done in similar situations to refine its path choices. Tesla noted that future v15 releases will expand that learning to cover the entire route rather than just the beginning and end segments.

Parking has been given meaningful updates as well. FSD now uses a driver's personal parking history to identify preferred spots at destinations they visit regularly, and the destination map can display multiple parking options simultaneously so drivers can compare before committing to one.

results.title: Tesla Starts FSD V15 Rollout, Adding Reality View and Speed-Camera Slowdown
results.content:
Tesla began rolling out version 15 of its Full Self-Driving software to a first wave of customers on Saturday, the company said on X, about 12 hours after Chief Executive Officer Elon Musk said the update would go to wide release next month.

“FSD v15 now starting to roll out – upgrading every part of the end-to-end driving network,” Tesla wrote.

Musk had written earlier on Saturday that “FSD V15 goes to wide release next month,” which EV covered. Saturday’s first wave comes ahead of that wider release.

## First Wave Only

Saturday’s release is a limited first stage, not the wide release Musk described.

“FSD v15 releasing to the first wave of customers today!!” Vice President of AI Software Ashok Elluswamy wrote shortly after the company’s post. [...] ## Navigation and Parking

V15 is the first FSD release to use Tesla’s own learned navigation, which Elluswamy described on the third-quarter call in October.

“Navigation for start & end of the trip now learns end-to-end from fleet route preferences,” Tesla said. “Later v15 releases will expand this to the entire route.”

That matches Elluswamy’s October remark that “the start and end of trips” would “already use this technology pretty soon as part of the V15 release.”

The AI account’s notes added “improved parking location selection by using personalized parking history.” The map “will now display multiple parking options at your destination,” they said.

## Potholes, Animals and Water [...] ## ‘Reality View’

The most visible change is a new on-screen view of the drive.

Tesla’s post says Tesla Reality View “adds a live visualization of the drive that lets you see & control what FSD is planning to do.”

The AI account’s notes called it a “new real-time generative driving visualization that continuously streams a view from an arbitrary virtual camera situated above your vehicle.”

Drivers can “select between fullscreen visualizations, maps or a split view – or choose quiet mode for a calming cabin experience,” the notes said. Upcoming navigation turns appear inside the visualization.

The notes also said V15 “introduced Tesla Reality View, replacing all of the explicit model signals into a single end-to-end visualization using less total compute.”
